node.title: Brace in the replacement part of a regular expression substitution
node.author: luc.bouge
node.doctext:
Dear monks

I have tried the following replacement script, which does not work.

$ more replace.pl #!/usr/bin/perl -w -pi.orig s/(a)(b)/$1{$2}/g; $ more test.txt ab $ ./replace.pl test.txt Use of uninitialized value within %1 in substitution iterator at ./replace.pl line 3, <> line 1. $ more test.txt (an empty line) However, it works fine with an additional escaping backslash before the left brace: s/(a)(b)/$1\{$2}/g;. I suspect that $1{$2} is recognized as addressing an associative array, but I could not find any mention in the documentation about such an expansion in the substitution part of a RE. Could somebody tell me? Regards, Luc.
